holes_in_opposing_case: The USD-higher/CAD-lower coalition (receive CORRA or long USDCAD) uses the wrong valuation denominator. Carry-is-king, rate-dove and positioning-cynic compare CRA 2027 implieds 3.13–3.595 to CORRA cash 2.29 and call 84–130.5bp of BoC hikes overpriced. Peer normalization is versus SOFR 3.85, SR3 2027-03/06 at 4.58/4.72, and US 2Y 4.76. Even after those CRA hikes, 2027 H1 CRA still sits about 140bp below SR3, matching CA-US 2Y at -140bp (3.77th percentile 1y, 4.31st percentile 5y). Receiving CORRA from that level fades a 4th-percentile peer dislocation; it does not harvest a rich Canadian path.

Carry-is-king’s claim that the energy/Fed-catch-up narrative is already in the 2027 CORRA path is false as a relative statement. CRA 2027-09 is +122bp from overnight versus SR3 2027-09 +90.5bp, yet the 2027 H1 strip gap remains ~140bp. Canada is priced to hike more than the US and still remain historically cheap. That is incomplete catch-up, not an overpaid story.

Positioning-cynic’s crowded BoC-hike book is not in the packet. CME positioning is unavailable and CORRA futures open interest is null, which that seat itself flags. The observable ownership fact is CFTC CAD leveraged-fund net -39022 as of 2026-09-15 at the 99.0th percentile of 1y net, weekly +16426 covering. That is a CAD-up flow headwind to CAD-lower expressions, not evidence that paying 2027 CORRA is crowded. A desk-thesis overlay is not a positioning check.

Dollar-king’s own USDCAD versus CA-US 2Y r-squared of 0.022 falsifies the incomplete-FX-translation pitch. A 4th-percentile rates gap with almost no mapping into spot is why the mispricing lives in SOFR-CORRA, not why one should buy USDCAD. Spot is only 74.0th percentile 1y / 87.0th 5y, still -1.25% over 3m, and the packet carry screen’s 140bp 2Y USD-over-CAD differential is the same cheap-Canada residual. Long USDCAD treats a rates dislocation as USD continuation and fights the covering already in CAD specs.

Rate-hawk and trend-follower pay SOFR into US 2Y 4.76 at the 99.8th percentile 1y after a delivered, >90%-priced 25bp hike, SOFR 3.85, and +57bp 1m. That is the already-rerated leg. Remaining 2027 residual is larger in Canada (CRA 2027-06 +107.5bp from 2.29) than in the US (SR3 2027-06 +87bp from 3.85). Paying the extreme US terminal while fading still-cheap Canada is the wrong relative. Outright US selloff analogs (2022-09-16) are why the expression is RV, not a license to pay Canada’s 4th-percentile discount.

Mean-reverter’s claim that the 156bp overnight SOFR-CORRA gap is an economic anchor, not an overshoot, fails the historical test. The same ~140bp prints in CA-US 2Y at the 4th percentile of both 1y and 5y windows and in 2027 H1 STIR (SR3 strip average 4.65 versus CRA 3.2475). Anchors do not sit in the 4th percentile after a delivered Fed hike and BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through. Closest level analog 2025-01-30 at -145bp compressed 25bp over 3m. Mean-reverter’s USD-lower/CAD-higher synopsis actually agrees with the FX implication; refusing the relative expression leaves the cheap Canada leg unowned.

Catalyst-junkie and perma-bear tag USD-up from an Australian housing/AONIA thesis while CAD is neutral or not_relevant. That is a USD residual of AUD-down. It does not value Canada versus the United States and does not touch CA-US 2Y -140bp, overnight 156bp, or 2027 H1 CRA versus SR3. An AU meeting-path or housing-channel trade is not a CA-US convergence argument.

Cross-merchant short AUDCAD agrees CAD higher and therefore does not refute CA-US compression. Rejecting rates because CA-AU 2Y is already 10.5th percentile 5y while AUDCAD is a 5y extreme is a different pair’s mapping error. AUDCAD at 0.997577 (99.8th/99.96th 1y/5y) is a commodity-peer FX flag of CAD cheapness, not evidence that a 140bp CA-US policy gap should persist.

Perma-bull pay-CORRA agrees with the Canada-catch-up leg. Neutral USD and CAD-higher is not an opposite rates-RV case. Outright long implied CORRA_2027-03 leaves the already-rerated US 2Y/SR3 unhedged after +57bp 1m. That is a worse expression of the same cheap-Canada view, not a reason to abandon the locked SOFR-CORRA 2027 H1 combo.
attack: Strongest opposing claim: Canada core near 2% (CPI-trim 1.9%/median 2.0%) and labor 38 with employment -42k mean the 84–130bp CRA hiking path is already too much, so USD stays higher and CAD stays lower via receive-CORRA or long USDCAD.

That claim prices Canada against itself. The market-implied assumption under attack is a persistent ~140bp Canada discount through 2027 H1, not whether CRA is above 2.29 cash. Activity gauges are close (CA 66 vs US 69); the rate gap dwarfs the inflation-gauge gap (55 vs 72). Labor softness is real and already in the packet, but it is the priced excuse for a 4th-percentile peer spread, not proof the spread is fair.

USD-up from AU housing (catalyst-junkie, perma-bear) or from paying an already 99.8th-percentile US 2Y (rate-hawk, trend-follower) does not close that peer gap. Dollar-king explicitly says the rates differential is already extreme and then uses that as a reason to buy spot; that is expression shopping around the dislocation, not a valuation of it.

Ownership and analog evidence cut against CAD-lower: CAD specs are covering, not initiating; 2025-01-30 from -145bp compressed 25bp over 3m. The 2024-12-18 analog that cheapened another 20bp is the falsifier already in the original invalidation, not a reason to receive CRA from 3.13/3.365.
defense: Valuation anchor unchanged: CA-US 2Y -140bp at the 4th percentile of both 1y and 5y history, triangulated by 2027 H1 SR3 minus CRA about 140bp and overnight SOFR-CORRA 156bp (3.85 vs 2.29). Percentile is the discovery flag; the disagreed assumption is the priced structural 140bp Canada discount after a delivered Fed hike and BoC energy pass-through minutes.

Convergence should begin now because the US leg has already rerated (US 2Y 4.76, 99.8th percentile 1y, +57bp 1m; SOFR jumped 3.62 to 3.85 on 17-Sep) while Canada 2Y is only 58.5th percentile 5y and CRA 2027-03/06 remain ~140bp through SR3. The 5d CA-US 2Y move of -15bp (z -2.17) after a >90%-priced FOMC is a new widening that known Canada-soft labor does not by itself explain.

Labor 38 and core near 2% remain the principal fundamental objection. Unknowns unchanged: Saudi Oman workaround may cap the energy tail; CME positioning and CA official curve are unavailable; 2024-12-18 analog from -130bp cheapened 20bp over 3m. Those are reasons for 70m of 100m gross, not for withdrawing or flipping to receive CORRA.

What would concede: next Canadian CPI/labor prints kill energy pass-through as a BoC issue, or CRA 2027-03/06 fail to reprice higher versus SR3 2027-03/06 and CA-US 2Y follows the 2024-12-18 widening analog rather than the 2025-01-30 compression analog. Outright US 2Y continuing to sell off is not by itself invalidation unless Canada cheapness widens.

Expression stays rates-first. Short USDCAD at 1.401047 is the same CAD-catch-up view but fights 140bp of 2Y carry, is only 74th/87th percentile, and dollar-king’s r-squared of 0.022 shows the FX mapping is not the mispricing. Rates candidate remains long SOFR 2027-03/06 versus short CORRA 2027-03/06. Sidecar open_positions is empty, so the book stays a new OPEN of that locked combo.

The closing mechanism is relative front-end repricing: CORRA implied rates rise versus SOFR as BoC catch-up and US 2Y already-extreme levels normalize the CA-US spread, rather than a generic USD-down or Canada-growth-up story.

context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: Canada headline CPI at 3% with core near 2%; US labor/inflation gauges still hot (75/72) versus Canada (38/55); Canada has been below the US on overnight and 2Y for months. New: the September 16 FOMC hike was >90% priced into the decision and has now printed, with SOFR jumping to 3.85; BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through; energy-market shock absorbers are weakening even as a Saudi Oman ship-to-ship workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail; desk thesis is that the energy shock is constraining global easing. The known Canada-soft labor picture cannot by itself explain a new 5d CA-US 2Y move of -15bp (z -2.17) after a US hike that was already widely expected.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: Pricing requires Canada to stay about 140bp cheap to the US through 2027 H1 even after CORRA prices more additional hikes than SOFR (CRA Sep-2027 +122bp versus SR3 Sep-2027 +90.5bp). Overnight CORRA-SOFR is 156bp (2.29 vs 3.85). That path assumes Canada core near 2% and labor weakness keep BoC structurally below the Fed, with energy pass-through remaining a minutes risk rather than a relative-rate event.

Percentile is the discovery flag; the disagreed assumption is the priced structural 140bp Canada discount.
